rfm_tuples.R: Implied: management commitment to PLMR equity through a -35% drawdown is consistent with strong fundamentals. The 10-K narrative emphasizes 'profitable since 2016', CAGR ~55% GWP growth, ROE 23.6%, and adoption of a new $200M share repurchase plan effective 2026-05-06.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B implied verification — if management truly believed PLMR was mispriced into the drawdown, Form 4 XML would show open-market PURCHASES (code P) by named C-suite or directors. Parse all 113 Form 4 filings since Dec 2024; classify codes (P = open-market purchase, S = open-market sale, M = option exercise, A = grant, F = sell-to-cover); separate discretionary vs mandatory sell-to-cover; check 10b5-1 plan adoption dates against pre/post-drawdown windows.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Across 113 Form 4 filings Dec 2024 – May 22 2026, code-P (open-market PURCHASE) count = 3, total dollar value = $132,942, and ALL THREE were by outside directors (Richard H. Taketa: 2x500-share buys 2025-08-18/19 at $120-121 = $121K combined; Martha Notaras: 100 shares 2025-08-07 at $119.92 = $12K). ZERO purchases by Chairman/CEO Mac Armstrong, President Jon Christianson, CFO Chris Uchida, COO Rodolphe Herve, CRO Jonathan Knutzen, CLO Angela Grant, or CPO Timothy Carter at any point in 18 months, including through the full -35% drawdown from peak. By contrast, code-S (open-market SALE) count = 165, total proceeds = $27,622,361, breakdown: Armstrong (CEO/Chair) $17,342,048 / 74 sales; Christianson (President) $4,622,810 / 26; Uchida (CFO) $3,668,608 / 32; Grant (CLO) $947,408; Knutzen (CRO) $738,931; Herve (COO) $198,881; Carter (CPO) $103,675. Aggregate insider sell:buy DOLLAR ratio = 208:1; C-suite-only sell:buy ratio is INFINITE (no C-suite purchases). Mac Armstrong adopted a 10b5-1 plan on 2025-12-03 covering sales 2026-03-23 to 2027-02-28; Uchida, Christianson, and Grant adopted plans 2025-12-15. CRITICAL TIMING: Armstrong's January 2026 sales (1/15: $300K, 1/21: $945K, 1/28-1/31: $2.3M) are NOT under any 10b5-1 plan (plan starts 2026-03-23) and cluster within the 10/27/2025 Gray Casualty signing → 1/27/2026 $300M term-loan close → 1/31/2026 acquisition consummation → 2/11/2026 Q4 earnings window. The 1/21/2026 sales ($945K at $127-130) are particularly discretionary — no RSU/PSU vesting event triggered them; they are not accompanied by 'mandatory sell-to-cover' footnotes that are present on Armstrong's RSU-tax sell-to-covers. After the Q1 2026 disclosure on 5/6/2026 (combined ratio jumping to 84.5%), Armstrong still sold $400K on 5/21/2026 — nominally under the 10b5-1 plan, but he did NOT pause or terminate the plan in response to deteriorating fundamentals. Across the entire 5-month drawdown window (Dec 2025 – May 2026), monthly insider proceeds: Dec'25 $917K, Jan'26 $4.87M, Feb'26 $816K, Mar'26 $422K, Apr'26 $1.87M, May'26 $583K — zero monthly NET buying.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the canonical Signal-OS honesty-alpha NEGATIVE pattern: a -35% drawdown in a self-described 'profitable since 2016, 55% CAGR' specialty insurer, with new $200M buyback authorization, but C-suite insiders are NET sellers of ~$27M with ZERO open-market conviction purchases. Two directors made token (<$130K total) purchases in August 2025 BEFORE the bulk of the drawdown — those are not 'into the weakness' buys. The contrast with the CALM ABG-pattern is stark: at PLMR there is no executive scaling-in. The most damning sub-finding is Armstrong's $945K discretionary January 2026 sale on 1/21 — outside any 10b5-1 plan, 6 days before the $300M term loan closed and 10 days before the acquisition consummation. Mode B catch: given the 10-K's deliberate framing of management commitment via the new $200M buyback, the absence of even a single management code-P is verifiable disconfirmation of the implied conviction narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'For the year ended December 31, 2025, our combined ratio was 76.9% compared to 78.1% in 2024 ... loss ratio of 28.5% in 2025 vs 26.4% in 2024 ... benefited from $19.8 million net favorable prior-year reserve development.' Issuer frames trajectory as continued underwriting profitability.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check FY2025 ratio trajectory against the most recent Q1 FY2026 10-Q (filed 2026-05-08) to test whether the issuer's 'continued profitability' narrative is consistent with the in-quarter trend, and decompose the loss-ratio change into mix vs accident-year.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 combined ratio = 84.5%, up 11.4 percentage points YoY from Q1 2025's 73.1%. Decomposition: loss ratio 33.3% (vs 23.6% prior Q1; +9.7pp), expense ratio 51.2% (vs 49.5%; +1.7pp). Catastrophe loss ratio was essentially zero in both quarters (0.1% vs -0.3%) — the entire jump is non-catastrophe attritional loss. Non-cat loss ratio = 33.2% vs 23.9% (+9.3pp). Q1 net income was FLAT at $42.9M ($42.947M vs $42.922M) despite GWP growing 42.4% YoY ($629.8M vs $442.2M). On adjusted basis (which excludes the $30M+ in transaction/amortization expenses booked for the Gray Casualty acquisition): adjusted combined ratio 76.0% Q1 2026 vs 68.5% Q1 2025 — still up 7.5pp. Adjusted ROE 26.6% vs 27.0% (essentially flat). Prior-year development was MORE favorable in Q1 2026 ($10.3M release) than Q1 2025 ($4.3M release) — i.e., the reported loss ratio benefited from an extra $6M of releases vs prior year, and the underlying accident-year loss ratio is even worse than the headline 33.3%. The Q3 2025 10-Q already showed YTD loss ratio at 32.3% vs 29.7% prior-year YTD — i.e., this trend has been visible for 3 quarters. Driver: product mix is rapidly shifting from Earthquake (38.3% of 2023 GWP → 33.9% 2024 → 28.2% 2025) to Casualty (7.9% → 15.3% → 26.8%; +130.5% YoY in 2025) plus newly acquired Surety/Credit. Casualty has structurally higher loss ratios than Earthquake.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's 'combined ratio 76.9%' headline obscures the in-quarter trajectory: by Q1 2026 the combined ratio had blown out to 84.5%, masked by continued favorable prior-year releases that are NOT sustainable. The non-cat loss ratio jump of +9.3pp in a single quarter, with no cat event, is the actual underlying story. Mode B catch: the 10-K's product-mix table makes the shift verifiable — Casualty went from 8% to 27% of GWP in 24 months — but the loss-ratio implications of that mix shift are not quantified in the 10-K narrative. The market is correctly pricing this as a structural margin compression, not a one-time event. Not severe because the data is fully disclosed and Q1 was not catastrophically unprofitable — still positive earnings.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K and 8-K (filed 2026-02-02, dated 2026-01-27/31): 'On January 31, 2026 ... the parties consummated the [Gray Casualty & Surety] Transaction ... for a purchase price of $300 million.' Funded via new January 2026 Credit Agreement: $300M Term Loan + $150M Revolver, maturing 2031-01-27. Issuer framing emphasizes 'expanded surety footprint' and 'A.M. Best A rating maintained.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify the leverage step-up, the timing relative to insider behavior, and whether the acquired entity is accretive on the issuer's actual margin metrics.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K + 8-K 2026-02-02 + Q1 FY2026 10-Q balance sheet/cash flow)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Balance sheet impact (Q1 FY2026 10-Q): Goodwill stepped up from $61.054M (Dec 2025) to $246.172M (Mar 2026) — a +$185M goodwill add for a $300M deal, i.e., ~62% of purchase price is goodwill/intangibles. New Term Loan outstanding: $297.4M (vs $0 prior). Interest expense $2.9M in Q1 alone, annualized ~$11.6M, against pre-deal annualized interest income tailwind. Q1 acquisitions, net of cash acquired = $246.3M of investing cash outflow. The deal was signed 10/27/2025 — the day after PLMR's stock had already started weakening from $135 peak. Term loan signed 1/27/2026 and deal closed 1/31/2026, in the same window Mac Armstrong was discretionarily selling $2.3M on 1/28-1/31. Gray Casualty contributed only $12.4M of Q1 GWP (PCSC line) and added $22.2M of acquired loss reserves; the 10-Q does not yet show whether Gray is accretive on a combined-ratio basis. The 10-K's discussion of Gray emphasizes strategic fit but does not quantify the IRR or the casualty-mix shift consequence. PLMR also separately acquired Advanced Ag Protection LLC (crop) for $29.5M in 2025 — stacked deals at the cyclical peak.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: the 10-K's framing of Gray Casualty as straightforward 'product expansion' understates the magnitude — first material debt on the balance sheet (~$297M term loan), large goodwill exposure ($185M added), purchase consummated in the same week the CEO was selling discretionarily, AND it pushes PLMR further into the Casualty mix that is already pressuring combined ratios. Not severe because the deal terms are fully disclosed, the leverage is moderate (~16% debt-to-capital, well within A.M. Best parameters), and PLMR has the surplus to absorb it. But this is a peak-of-cycle, peak-of-stock-price, debt-funded M&A pivot away from Earthquake — a meaningful capital-allocation signal that the market has correctly down-rated.

rfm_tuples.R: 8-K filed 2026-05-06: 'On April 30, 2026, the Company's Board of Directors approved the adoption of a share repurchase plan ... that authorizes the purchase of up to $200 million of the outstanding shares of Company common stock, as conditions warrant, with a term of two years from the effective date. Upon the effectiveness of the Plan, the Company's existing share repurchase plan was terminated.' Framed by management as deployment of capital into weakness.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — if the new $200M authorization signals genuine conviction in PLMR's intrinsic value, examine actual Q1 2026 repurchase pace (when stock was already weak) to test whether the company was buying aggressively or restrained, and whether the predecessor program was being meaningfully utilized.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q1 FY2026 10-Q Stockholders Equity note + financing cash flow)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Under the predecessor $100M July 2025 program, PLMR repurchased only 190,255 shares for $23.1M in Q1 2026 at an avg $121.33. That left $89.6M still available under the predecessor program when the Board cancelled it on 4/30 and issued a new $200M program. In other words, the existing authorization was only ~10% utilized in 9 months even while the stock dropped from $135 to ~$120 in Q1, and was barely 10% utilized BEFORE the additional drawdown to ~$92-100 in late April/May. The 'new $200M plan' announcement is largely an accounting reset rather than a step-change in pace; if conviction were strong, the company could have aggressively used the unutilized $89.6M into the Q1-end weakness. Cash used in Q1 2026 financing: $97.4M acquisition-related + $23.1M buyback; cash used in investing: $373.4M (mostly Gray Casualty). Cash deployed to deals (~$246M Gray + $30M Crop) is ~10x cash deployed to buybacks during the drawdown.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch on the buyback-as-conviction-signal narrative. The 4/30 $200M re-authorization is being read by media as bullish, but the actual Q1 pace was only ~$23M into clear weakness, and the predecessor program was largely unused. Combined with zero C-suite open-market purchases, the buyback is more capital-allocation theater than conviction. Not severe because buybacks are still occurring and the authorization is real; but it materially weakens the bull-case interpretation of the 'new $200M plan'.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q: 'The Company experienced favorable prior year development of $10.3 million ... during the three months ended March 31, 2026 ... primarily due to lower than anticipated severity of attritional losses in the Company's Inland Marine and Property line of business.' 2025 full-year: $19.8M favorable. 2024: $3.0M favorable. Issuer frames these as evidence of conservative reserving.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify the magnitude of reserve releases as a percentage of in-quarter net income and check whether the favorable-development cushion is durable given the mix shift to longer-tail Casualty.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Reserve Development tables + Q1 FY2026 Note 5)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 $10.3M favorable PYD vs pretax income of $53.5M — i.e., PYD contributed ~19% of pretax income. Without the $6M YoY incremental favorable PYD (Q1 2026 $10.3M vs Q1 2025 $4.3M), Q1 2026 pretax income would have been ~$47.5M and EPS ~$1.39 vs reported $1.57 — a meaningful flatter. Underlying accident-year loss ratio (incurred + PYD reversed): current-year losses $97.4M on net earned premiums $261.4M = 37.3% pure accident-year loss ratio, vs 27.5% prior-year-ex-PYD. The PYD has been concentrated in Inland Marine/Property (the segment shrinking as % of GWP) while Casualty (the rapidly growing segment) is longer-tail and the early reserves on Casualty may not release favorably for 2-5 years — if at all.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The reported combined-ratio expansion is actually understated. Without the increasing favorable PYD cushion (which is structurally non-recurring as mix shifts to Casualty), the underlying accident-year combined ratio is closer to 88-89%, not the headline 84.5%. Mode B: the 10-K notes the PYD comes from Inland Marine/Property, which is in run-off as a percentage of book; the new Casualty book has no proven release pattern yet. This is a 'borrowing from the future' dynamic the market is increasingly pricing in.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors: 'Our insurance operations expose us to claims arising from unpredictable catastrophe events, such as earthquakes, hurricanes, droughts, windstorms, floods, wildfires, and other severe events ... California ... represented 30.9% of GWP for 2025.' Risk language is qualitative; no specific quantification of California wildfire net retention.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — California is PLMR's largest state (30.9% GWP) and earthquake is its largest single product (28.2%); verify whether wildfire exposure within the inland marine/HO book is meaningfully disclosed, and whether the 1:250 PML disclosure ($20M net retention) actually covers wildfire as well as earthquake.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Item 1 Reinsurance + Item 1A Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K confirms net retention is $20.0M for earthquake events and $11.0M for hurricane events 'and all other perils' — wildfire falls under 'all other perils' with the $11M tower attaching at $3.1B for earthquake and only $100M for continental U.S. hurricane. Wildfire-specific limits and PML are NOT separately disclosed in the 10-K. California-specific (Earthquake + Homeowners + Hawaii Hurricane + Inland Marine) is now 30.9% of book or ~$626M GWP. The Q1 2026 favorable PYD was driven by attritional Inland Marine losses being LOWER than expected — not by avoided catastrophe events. PLMR did not report any specific California wildfire impact in Q1 2026 ($268K total cat losses for the quarter).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Wildfire exposure to PLMR's $626M California book is qualitatively disclosed but not quantified at a useful granularity. Within the cutoff and using only EDGAR sources, I cannot verify (a) PLMR's actual California wildfire PML, (b) whether the $11M 'all other perils' tower has been tested against a major California wildfire scenario at scale, or (c) the geographic concentration of PLMR's CA homeowners book relative to known WUI zones. UNVERIFIABLE within blinded EDGAR-only constraints. Flag for follow-up via NAIC SERFF or PLMR's CA DOI filings.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Armstrong's pre-10b5-1-effective discretionary sales: 2025-12-22 (4 line items, $681K total, 1 day before quarter close); 2026-01-21 (4 line items aggregating 5,000 shares, $945K total at $127-130, NO sell-to-cover footnote, NO RSU vesting on that date — these are pure discretionary open-market sales 6 days before the $300M term loan closed); 2026-02-12 (8 line items, $613K, 1 day after Q4 earnings release). His 1/28-1/31 sales ARE sell-to-cover associated with PSU/RSU vesting (cleared by mandatory withholding footnotes). Combined Dec 22 - Feb 12 discretionary window: ~$2.24M of CEO discretionary sales clustering exactly around the M&A close + earnings release windows, all PRIOR to his 10b5-1 plan's 2026-03-23 effective sale start. None of these were blackout-period violations per se (PLMR's policy may permit window-period trading), but they are not 10b5-1-defense-protected. After the bad Q1 print on 5/6, Armstrong did NOT pause his 10b5-1 plan and sold another $400K on 5/21 at $113-115.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Mode-B catch here is the strongest single finding in the file. The 10-K's Item 9B Rule 10b5-1 disclosure NAMES the four insider plans adopted in Dec 2025, BUT specifies that sales under Armstrong's plan only BEGIN 2026-03-23 — a 4-month gap during which any sale is discretionary, not 10b5-1-protected. Cross-referencing the Form 4 XML shows the CEO did in fact make ~$2.2M in discretionary, non-sell-to-cover sales in that gap window, clustering at the Q4 quarter-close (12/22), 6 days before the M&A debt close (1/21), and the day after Q4 earnings (2/12). This is the asymmetric sell:buy + pre-bad-news clustering pattern the framework's insider_vs_calendar m-source is specifically designed to detect, and it escalates the form4 finding from RED_FLAG to SEVERE. The framework spec's instruction: 'If Form 4 evidence directly contradicts the issuer's narrative ... clustered selling pre-bad-news, opposite of management's confidence framing — escalate to SEVERE' — applies here.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K and Q1 FY2026 10-Q: 'Beginning in 2026, the Company has updated the categorization of its products to align with management's current strategy and view of the business. Prior year amounts have been reclassified for comparability purposes ... Fronting Premium will cease to be reported as a separate line of business and the underlying premium will be consolidated into existing lines.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — mid-cycle product recategorization should be examined for whether it materially obscures year-over-year comparisons in the deteriorating loss-ratio narrative, particularly given that Fronting was historically a lower-margin / pass-through line being subsumed into other categories.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K product mix tables + Q1 2026 10-Q segment note (1))
rfm_tuples.M_value: The 2026 recategorization breaks out Surety & Credit as a separate line (5.1% of Q1 2026 GWP) and consolidates Fronting into other lines (Fronting was 18.6% of 2024 GWP, declining to 9.4% in 2025 due to a partnership termination in Q3 2024, and now disappears from external reporting). Combined with the 2025 retroactive reclassification of Casualty (which now includes E&S Casualty + Surety + Environmental Liability), this is the second material product-segment re-cut in 18 months. Specifically, the Casualty product line jumped from 7.9% of GWP in 2023 to 26.8% in 2025 — partly real growth, partly reclassification. The new presentation makes 2026 vs 2025 vs 2024 line-item comparison difficult without doing the recast math from the 10-K's appendix tables.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Not strictly deceptive — the changes are disclosed, the prior periods are recast, and the rationale (a real strategic shift away from low-margin Fronting and toward Casualty/Surety after the Gray acquisition) is plausible. But the timing of the recategorization — coincident with the loss-ratio deterioration and the M&A pivot — makes it harder for analysts to cleanly track the trend the market is reacting to. Mode B catch: the issuer's framing of 'continued underwriting profitability' is partly underwritten by the obscuring effect of the product-line redefinitions. Not severe; rated MODERATE because PLMR did provide recast tables, but the practical effect is to muddy the comparability of the trend.

summary: PLMR is the cleanest honesty-alpha negative pattern in the forward test so far. Despite a self-described 'profitable since 2016, 55% CAGR, ROE 23.6%' specialty insurer narrative and a fresh $200M buyback authorization, Form 4 XML across 113 filings shows ZERO open-market C-suite PURCHASES through a -35% drawdown — only $133K of token director buys in Aug 2025 (pre-drawdown) against $27.6M of insider sales. The Mode-B catch escalates this to SEVERE: CEO Mac Armstrong's Rule 10b5-1 plan (adopted 2025-12-03) only authorizes sales beginning 2026-03-23, yet ~$2.2M of his sales between 12/22/2025 and 2/12/2026 are NOT sell-to-cover and NOT plan-protected — they cluster at the Q4 quarter-close, 6 days before the $300M term loan closed for the Gray Casualty acquisition, and the day after Q4 earnings. Layered on top: Q1 2026 combined ratio jumped to 84.5% (vs 73.1% prior) on non-catastrophe attritional losses driven by the rapid mix shift from Earthquake (38% → 28%) to Casualty (8% → 27%); the headline ratio is flattered by ~$10M of favorable PYD that is structurally not durable as the book lengthens; and $246M cash + $297M new term debt was deployed on Gray Casualty at the price peak. Combined verdict: SHORT-tier.
